header:
Date: 2026-02-09
Start: 15:30 PST
Duration: 63 minutes
Attendees: Ethan Park (Redwood AE), Maya Johnson (Redwood SE), Daniel Ruiz (Redwood CSM); Laura Chen (Cypress Procurement), Samir Patel (Cypress Security), Nadia Gomez (Cypress Legal), Priya Rao (Cypress Eng), Tommy Lee (Cypress FinOps)
summary: Kickoff to align procurement, security and engineering on vendor onboarding. Discussed MSA/DPA redline priorities, privileged keying (KMS) options, SSO/SAML, and an initial acceptance/runbook for a short pilot. Redwood to provide SOC2 and a focused perf baseline. Customer flagged egress fees and model variance as gating items.
topics: Privileged keying / KMS options (bring-your-own vs Redwood-managed)
SLA tiers and rollout plan for pilot
Pricing egress concerns and FinOps thresholds
Technical preflight: VPC peering, KV cache, seq-length expectations
transcript:
[00:00] Ethan (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I think we have about an hour, is that right?
[00:06] Laura (Cypress Procurement): Yup that's right. Thanks, Ethan. We're short on time so want to make sure we hit the legal asks first.
[00:12] Ethan: Perfect. Quick roll call — Maya is our SE, Daniel on CSM, and from Cypress we have Laura, Samir, Nadia, Priya, and Tommy. Cool.
[00:22] Nadia (Cypress Legal): Right, the team circulated the draft MSA yesterday. We flagged a few DPA items and a privilege keying clause — basically we need clarity on customer-managed KMS and key escrow.
[00:34] Maya (Redwood SE): Sure, happy to walk through options. Redwood supports three patterns: hosted keys (Redwood-managed), customer KMS passthrough (bring-your-own in the control plane), and full on-prem private where keys never leave customer control. There was a small — sorry — there can be nuance with log redaction and audit logs.
[00:53] Samir (Security): When you say passthrough, is that direct HSM handshake or are you proxying calls? We need to know if Redwood ever sees plaintext keys or unwrapped data.
[01:03] Maya: Good question. For our KMS integration we do a key unwrap flow within a customer VPC option — in that mode Redwood doesn't persist key materials; we exchange wrapped keys, and the runtime performs unwrap in an ephemeral host. I should note sometimes our docs call that "privileged key path" — could be misread as 'privy' in older notes.
[01:22] Samir: Ok, ephemeral only is fine but we need a diagram and an attestation flow.
[01:28] Ethan: We'll add a network diagram to the SOC2 bundle. Maya, can you also produce a simple sequence showing unwrap/usage and TTL?
[01:36] Maya: Yep I can.
[01:38] Tommy (FinOps): Side note on pricing — egress fees are a big worry for us. The model footprint and per-token billing plus egress from restricted regions is gonna impact total cost. Does Redwood have a typical egress mitigation pattern?
[01:51] Daniel (Redwood CSM): A lot of customers use region pinning and local caching for high-volume endpoints to reduce egress. We also recommend model quantization and batching to lower token counts. We can show an example runbook later.
[02:08] Priya (Eng): For the pilot we expect bursty RPS — maybe 120 RPS at 4–6 second conversational seq lengths and occasional 8k seq for long retrievals. How does that map to Dedicated vs Hosted?
[02:21] Maya: With that profile, Dedicated GPUs with a small burst pool is the cleanest path. Hosted can work but you'd see more tail latency variance and throttling at scale, unless we reserve capacity.
[02:33] Priya: Got it. We need SLOs for 95th and 99th percentile.
[02:37] Ethan: We'll propose SLA targets for both Dedicated and Hosted, with explicit rollback to cheaper model variants if latency SLOs are violated.
[02:45] Nadia: On the legal side, two asks: one, we need an indemnity carveout clarified for data processed in plugin/tool calls; two, retention windows — the DPA needs explicit 30/90/365 options.
[02:57] Ethan: We can map retention tiers to product plans. I'll flag which plans keep prefix cache and which expire token-level logs at 30 days.
[03:07] Nadia: Also we might ask for a narrow SOC 2 addendum for privileged access reviews quarterly.
[03:11] Ethan: Okay, addendum is doable — we'll include audit cadence.
[03:14] Laura: Timeline wise procurement wants legal signoff for pilot by EOW — end of next week. Is that realistic?
[03:21] Priya: Engineering needs the perf benchmark first to validate cost assumptions.
[03:24] Ethan: Agreed. Proposed path: Redwood shares SOC2 + KMS diagram by Tuesday, Maya runs a focused perf baseline (we'll spin up a dedicated 1-GPU small pool) and share numbers by Monday next week, Nadia sends prioritized MSA redlines by Friday, procurement to review and aim to sign pilot MSA by next Friday.
[03:42] Samir: For the attestation we will need a signed runbook and the network peering IP ranges, plus an assurance we won't see plaintext message logs in any retention.
[03:52] Maya: We'll include a runbook and redact-in-transit patterns; note that for certain function-calling flows we do capture structured outputs — we can flag those fields as non-persistent.
[04:05] Nadia: We'll also want to check if Redwood supports SAML provisioning — SSO for admin console.
[04:10] Ethan: Yes, SAML/SCIM is supported — we will share the SSO integration checklist.
[04:16] Tommy: On pricing approvals, is there a committed spend option to reduce per-token rates for the pilot?
[04:21] Ethan: We can offer a small committed monthly credit for Dedicated pilot customers; I'll include a proposed rate card.
[04:28] Priya: One more technical — any constraints on KV cache eviction and sequence reuse? Our retrieval system expects stable KV across a session.
[04:35] Maya: KV cache is per-session and we can pin policy to keep prefixes for N minutes; persistence across restarts is not guaranteed outside Dedicated pools. We'll document recommended TTLs.
[04:47] Laura: This is helpful. Quick request: can Redwood provide a short one-page 'acceptance criteria' listing required deliverables for a pilot? We want a clear gate.
[04:56] Ethan: Absolutely — we'll include acceptance criteria: security docs, perf pass, SLA targets, redline resolution.
[05:02] Nadia: And legal will prepare a prioritized redline doc — expecting to send by Friday.
[05:06] Ethan: Great. Any other blockers?
[05:08] Priya: None from engineering beyond the perf numbers.
[05:11] Samir: Security wants the attestation diagram and ephemeral key proof.
[05:15] Ethan: We'll action those.
[05:17] Daniel: I'll open a Confluence playbook and share links in the follow-up email.
[05:20] Laura: Perfect. Thanks everyone.
[05:23] Ethan: Thanks — recap in an email with next steps.
[05:27] [crosstalk and brief goodbyes]
[05:33] End of recording
